_: Evaluation set for code retrieval (BACKLOG rag-code-retrieval-quality).
Each question is phrased the way an agent asks one when it does NOT already know the symbol:
a concept, a symptom, a responsibility. That constraint is the whole point — a question that
contains the identifier is a question grep answers better, and including such questions would
let a change look like an improvement while making the tool no more useful than `grep -rn`.
`grep_beats_it` records, honestly, whether a plausible literal grep would find the answer
faster anyway. Questions marked true are NOT failures when retrieval loses them; they are here
so the set cannot drift into measuring only the cases retrieval happens to win.
`answer` is a chunk-id substring. Ids are `path#kind name`, so naming the file and the item
pins the answer without depending on how the id is spelled in full.
SECOND BAND, added 2026-08-31: questions whose answers sat at ranks 2-29 rather than at 1
or beyond reach. The first twenty could not see a ranking change at all — every answer was
already in top-5 or unreachable — so slot composition improving 54 to 80 of 100 registered
as no movement whatever. A metric blind to the change it is meant to judge is worse than no
metric, because it reads as evidence of nothing happening.
